items.summary:
Do NOT spend on this game until the devs reverted all their recent changes, if they don't it'll probably EoS anyway and that money is gone-gone.

I used to recommend this game to everyone and got around 10 people to start playing it. Now I wouldn't recommend it to a single soul, the devs have outed themselves as typical gacha devs, you can't play units you want anymore and clear content, they will change/powercreep mechanics to force your spending, and worst of all - they will take in zero of the feedback and completely f over the players who kept them afloat when the game was about to EoS 2 years ago.

items.title: [负面] The game is great. I really love the diverse chara...
items.summary: The game is great. I really love the diverse characters, their unique playstyles, the engaging story filled to the brim with references to lovecraft, beautiful art, and f2p friendly nature. Until the recent 2.6 changes to the endgame mode D-tide (making it so that certain characters that could do percent based damage and cheese or meta strats being manditory to clear the highest level and removing a lower difficulty level), how they would conveniently "fix" the corpo+horla WoD combo right after running their banners back to back effectively nerfing the character right after you got everyone to pull her, and nerfing affinity leveling to hell, effectively forcing people to buy the tokens to skip levels for an insane amount of rose script. In this state I cannot recommend you spend any money, or if this continues, time, on this game as they are actively adding more things to push the player base into whaling or being left behind.

Last patch messed up the game. Morimens used to be one of the friendliest Gachas out there. I used to recommend it for people to try, but not anymore with the recent update 2.6. Lots of unnecessary nerfs just after the rerun of said nerfed characters, and D-Tide seems to be an untested mess. Recently released characters become barely useful.

I was hoping for more balance, but it seems that the game is heading in another direction.

items.title: [负面] This review may or may not change in the future, d...
items.summary:
This review may or may not change in the future, depending if the developers continue to disregard feedback from the players.

As beautiful and as fun as it was, I can only recommend playing the game if you enjoy the story. I wouldn't currently recommend supporting the game financially as it is now.

The game grows more anti-consumer and predatory as the developers ignore valid feedback. Unnecessary "bug fixes" were made to a character who wasn't even considered meta, and recently, changes were made to a major endgame mode that turned it into a SLOGFEST of whaling and cheesing (instead of making changes to the gamemodes that ACTUALLY needed changes such as P-Dive and Hectic Skybound Rail). After complaints, the developers' response was a nothingburger and barely brought up the issue. They later sent out 100 version-locked gacha currency as compensation (though it felt more like hush-money).

The purchasable features / packs and gacha in the game in general have already felt quite predatory, though my main problem with the game as of recently is the changes to gameplay making it a lot less enjoyable for free-to-play and low-spending players.

items.title: [负面] I found this game recently via random Youtube reco...
items.summary:
I found this game recently via random Youtube recommendations.

TL;DR: While I have had a lot of fun, and am likely to keep playing for at least a little while longer, I cannot recommend the game in its current state. In particular, I would [i]actively]/i] discourage giving this game any money. The developers have shown a habit of subjecting the players to bait-and-switches, running character banners only to nerf those characters (directly or indirectly) [i]immediately[/i] afterwards. The game balance is also abysmal, to the point I don't think it can even be accurately called that.

For a more comprehensive list of issues:

1. With standard banner characters, the recommended mission level is about 5 levels higher than it needs to be (as in, a level 20 team can take on a level 25 challenge without too much effort). With limited banner characters, that discrepancy goes up to 10-20 levels. What this means is that getting all of the achievements with standard characters at the right level is trivial. With limited banner characters, even just [i]one[/i] on the team will result in eliminating bosses in one turn and sometimes one [i]card[/i], or else trivialize surviving against the boss indefinitely. For early story, having more than one on a team is entirely superfluous.

2. To combat this level of power creep, later stages and game modes have recently had bosses changed to have in some cases around a hundred times the HP pool they used to, and to deal massively inflated damage. This is instead of, but also sometimes in addition to, properly challenging mechanics.

3. The result of those two factors means that people who don't invest an absurd amount of time and money into the game can expect to not be able to win at all in late-game. You cannot get the things needed without both.

4. On top of all of this, limited characters have in multiple instances been rendered obsolete via nerfs (or "bug fixes" for "bugs" the developers had openly stated they were aware of [i]well[/i] before the character banner rerun, but had no intention to fix until after) immediately after a banner for them was run, resulting in everyone who grabbed them because they were a meta pick (or even, in the most recent case, because the character was fun and only moderately strong) getting scammed.

5. In order to unlock side stories, you have to use a limited resource of which you get one per day (up to 3 if you pay). Each side story chapter costs between 3 and 7 of that resource. Even to unlock just the [i]essential[/i] side story chapters that shouldn't even be side story, you have to do your dailies for around a month. If you go through the main story quickly, you'll have to either stop and wait for days to a week in the middle to get the requisite side story chapters, or skip them and come back later, resulting in missing information for later main chapters and lackluster experiences of those side chapters due to distance from the intended point of playing.

6. The essential side story chapters are not listed anywhere except in community guides. There is no official resource that distinguishes the necessary side chapters from the unnecessary ones. At least one side story chapter is also placed in the wrong place in the official guide, meaning following that will cause you to be exposed to spoilers for later in the main story, and this has been a known issue for at least 9 months and still has not been fixed.

7. Characters belong to one of four "realms", each of which grants a specific effect. Recent new limited characters alter the realms they belong to, in 3/4 cases making the realms objectively worse, and it has been stated that [i]all[/i] new characters will do this.

8. The PvP mode has been effectively abandoned, allegedly due to lacking manpower, but given the other decisions being made, I have to doubt the veracity of that claim.

9. Character affinity is a gauge of how much a given character likes you. Leveling it up gets you resources and the characters' stories. Affinity gain was recently altered, and now it can be expected that it will take up to a year to level [i]one[/i] character's affinity. If you like a specific character and want to know more about them, be ready for a [i]long[/i] grind.

10. The developers frequently ask for player feedback, but evidently do not read any of it. It genuinely seems like a complete waste of time to mention issues in the feedback forms or the Discord server. If you get any response, it will be at most a lukewarm "We'll look into it" with no future action.

11. In the late-game, at present, you can expect there to be 3-4 viable builds. This is a new development; there used to be much more freedom with team building while still allowing competitive performance.

In short, if you do decide to play this game, any money you spend can be safely assumed to retroactively be made a waste shortly thereafter. Please refrain until the developers show that they can be trusted, because at present there is no evidence they can be.

Points 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 are all personal issues I take with the game in its current state, but are echoed in the community. The others are issues that are widely complained about in the community, and, having watched others play the game, I full-heartedly agree with those complaints.
